type: Cranium-informed macro + holdings + watchlist rate-sensitivity overlay
evidencePolicy: Cranium supplied the research questions, source URLs and sell-side disagreements. Facts below were independently checked where material. Qualitative stock sensitivities are Power Stack synthesis and are not fundamental score changes.

coreResearchFrames: Fed ambiguity is itself a pricing variable; Morgan Stanley's attached piece has HOLD as the September base case, not hike.
Long-end yields can remain restrictive even if the Fed holds; do not equate hold with easier financial conditions.
AI financing method and long-end yields are now part of the AI-capex thesis, not an external macro footnote.
Low index/rates volatility plus lower put protection can underprice a wide macro outcome distribution.
China bank/insurer recapitalisation and China 'alternative AI beta' are separate mechanisms; neither proves domestic macro repair.
Energy risk can migrate from headline crude into gas, refined products, shipping and power.

US.regime: Restrictive long-end and real yields; September policy outcome still genuinely ambiguous ahead of CPI/PPI.
verifiedReadings: Sep 4 US Treasury references: 2Y ~4.37%, 10Y ~4.78%, 30Y ~5.24%; 10Y real yield ~2.43-2.45%.
Fed September hike probability was about 57% in current Sep 7 reporting after the jobs report.
Brent was around $97 and WTI around $92 on Sep 7, keeping the inflation tail active.
CPI and PPI are the decisive pre-FOMC inflation tests; the Sep FOMC is Sep 15-16.
US.craniumInterpretation: The important distinction is front-end policy ambiguity versus already-restrictive long-end financing. A hold can still be bearish for duration if inflation credibility, Treasury supply/buybacks or term-premium pressure keep the 10Y/30Y high.

China.regime: Very low sovereign yields and unchanged benchmark lending rates coexist with weak domestic credit demand. Current support is more balance-sheet/fiscal than a fresh PBOC easing cycle.
verifiedReadings: August 1Y LPR held at 3.00% and 5Y LPR at 3.50% for a 15th consecutive month.
China 10Y government yield was below 1.7% in early September, more than 300bp below US Treasuries.
Loan growth slowed to a record-low 5.1% in July in current Reuters/Breakingviews reporting.
Beijing is recapitalising major state banks and insurers with roughly CNY360-365bn / ~$54bn of capital support, including ICBC and Agricultural Bank.
The recap improves solvency/lending capacity and supports long-term equity investment, but weak credit demand means transmission into the real economy is not guaranteed.
Q2 GDP growth slowed to 4.3%; domestic investment/demand remained weak while exports and AI-linked manufacturing stayed comparatively resilient.
China.craniumInterpretation: China is the mirror image of the US rates problem. The US problem is expensive money. China's problem is cheap money with weak demand and weak transmission. Lower Chinese yields help duration/funding mathematically, but can simultaneously signal deflationary pressure, trapped savings and poor private credit demand. Bank recapitalisation should therefore be tracked separately from rate cuts.

macroSweep.crossMarketConclusion: Do not use one global 'rates up/down' tag. US rate sensitivity is predominantly discount-rate/financing stress; China sensitivity must combine low yields with credit-demand weakness, state balance-sheet support and CNY transmission.

portfolioImplications: Do not broadly de-risk the physical AI/grid sleeve solely because rates are high; instead separate funded backlog/cash conversion (ETN/PWR/YTLPOWR/FLEX) from long-duration narrative exposure (SMR, MSTR, higher-beta robotics).
Within current holdings, the clearest rate-risk concentration is TSLA + TTWO + YTLPOWR/6742UW. XOM/HIBISCS/MISC are more exposed to China demand and energy-flow changes than to the US discount rate.

Within the watchlist, the highest US-rate/liquidity fragility is MSTR, SMR, COIN/BTC, GDXJ and high-growth automation/software. Quality operating scarcity names such as CCJ, LHX and cash-generative energy/agriculture are less directly duration-sensitive.

China's bank recap should raise attention on CSI/onshore AI optionality and state-backed power/equipment names, but it does not yet justify promoting broad China cyclicals. Confirmation is credit creation, breadth and earnings, not the recap headline itself.
FCX, BG/NTR/AGCO, LNG/SLB and China/HK automation are the watchlist names where China macro/credit demand has the most direct fundamental read-through.
No fundamental score change is justified by the rates sweep alone. This overlay changes macro risk ranking and what evidence must be demanded before adding.
